system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note do **not** establish Buyer agreement. All positions remain subject to review. The recommendations below use the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free baseline; underlying DD documents and the complete SPA have not been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general warranty cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter:** open at 100% of price, negotiating the general cap against diligence and available security; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for protected claim categories. | **Counter:** propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket, recovering qualifying claims from dollar one once triggered; Seller’s structure leaves Buyer bearing recurring losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, preserving timely notified claims and separate longer periods elsewhere. | **Amend:** seek 24–36 months and reject universal application; Buyer needs adequate post-Completion reporting cycles to discover claims. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Separate capacity, authority and title protections: at least price-level cap, no thresholds and longer survival. | **Reject:** seek a 100% price cap and six-year contractual notification period, subject to NSW limitation/deed advice; ownership defects threaten the whole investment. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception supplied. | Express protection for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, including relevant Seller representatives; preserve non-excludable statutory rights. | **Insert overriding carve-out:** disapply caps, contractual time bars, thresholds, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions to fraud; Seller must not contractually shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referred-to matters, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair, sufficiently detailed disclosure identifying the nature and scope of exceptions to identified warranties; a frozen, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deeming:** require specific cross-references and exclude automatic qualification of indemnities and fundamental protections; document availability is not meaningful disclosure of risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Any Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable in data room or public records, defeats claims. | No knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal personnel, without constructive or imputed knowledge. | **Delete or tightly narrow:** exclude adviser imputation and any duty to investigate; Seller should not shift warranty risk through hypothetical discoverability. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite outstanding evidence of conditions. | A Buyer-waivable Completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable amendments, fees or termination rights. | **Make a substantive CP:** verify the executed consent and every associated condition before Completion; approximately 30% of revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, repayment through Completion funds flow and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion. | **Reject unsecured post-close delivery:** require binding discharge arrangements and deduct repayment from Seller proceeds consistently with price mechanics; Buyer must receive a debt-free, unencumbered business without double-counting. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses are “for Seller” but absent from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Express Seller economic responsibility for transaction bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with correct payroll handling. | **Itemise and fund:** deduct or reserve the applicable amounts from Seller proceeds and obtain an indemnity, avoiding double-counting; calling them Seller liabilities does not prevent the acquired company paying them. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is recorded open and transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. | Verified settlement of all relevant fees, effective assignment and a broader indemnity for losses from pre-Completion ownership defects and related claims. | **Require cure plus protection:** obtain payment evidence and confirmatory assignment, backed by a ring-fenced indemnity; paying one identified invoice may not establish complete IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unknown. | Prompt investigation, containment, evidence preservation, legal assessment of notification obligations and protection for pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Keep open:** require investigation deliverables and remediation covenants, plus a specific indemnity and consider retention; uncertainty supports protection, not a finding of either immateriality or confirmed breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Combined review of timing, scope, cancellation rights, accruals and commercial benefit, with correct working-capital/debt treatment. | **Investigate before allocating:** restrict new non-ordinary-course commitments and adjust price only where justified; neither ordinary-course status nor Seller liability is established. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | All-Claims wording spreads limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance across the agreement. | Express separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and price/payment obligations, with overriding fraud protection. | **Rewrite scope and precedence:** apply each limitation only to its intended category and preserve appropriate remedies; broad definitions could silently defeat negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller holding 100%. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital, share classes, transfers, certificates, options/convertibles, encumbrances and Seller authority. | **Verify before Completion:** obtain supporting corporate records, searches, releases and valid transfer/registration deliverables; the register alone does not establish unencumbered title to all equity interests. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP are considered settled under the general regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with appropriate assessment-period survival and exceptions; robust IP ownership, infringement and licensing warranties with tailored limits and Ironquay protection. | **Reopen expressly:** negotiate tax and IP scope, caps, survival and exclusions separately; Seller’s assertion of settlement does not address their distinct exposure or discovery periods. |

**Completion priorities:** effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonus funding, Ironquay ownership cure and verified share title. Keep incident investigation and supplier-renewal diligence open pending evidence.
=== END ADVICE ===
